note: User word 'βγδa' contains Greek characters; the English rules (dictionary.c TranslateRules) emit phonSWITCH followed by the alphabet language 'el' into word_phonemes (p). This is the tainted input that drives the translator2 switching logic.
SetTranslator2("el") allocates the secondary translator translator2 (Greek) and records translator2_language = "el".
translator2 (Greek) is passed as the active translator 'tr' of a nested TranslateWord/TranslateWord3 call that is still executing when translator2 is later freed.

code: wordx += TranslateLetter(tr, wordx, unpron_phonemes, non_initial, current_alphabet);
note: The Greek translator treats 'βγδa' as unpronounceable (no Greek vowel in the first letters), so letters are spelled one by one; 'tr' here is the Greek translator2 and the Latin letter 'a' is about to be spelled.

The Latin letter 'a' has no letter-name in the Greek translator (ph_buf[0]==0) and its alphabet language is 'en', so SetTranslator2("en") is invoked re-entrantly while 'tr' is still the Greek translator2.

new_language "en" differs from translator2_language "el", so SetTranslator2 deletes the Greek translator object even though it is still the active 'tr' of the enclosing nested TranslateWord call (use-after-free root cause).
After SetTranslator2 freed translator2, the nested TranslateLetter continues and reads tr->phoneme_tab_ix from the freed Greek translator: heap-use-after-free read.
